item.title: [fastapi/fastapi] 0.149.0
item.description:
Browsers submit empty text inputs as empty strings (`""`). FastAPI now treats empty scalar form values as missing in form models, matching individual `Form` parameters. Required fields return a validation error. Fields with defaults or default factories use them and remain unset in `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`.
Empty strings inside lists are preserved. Omitted boolean form fields still become `False`. JSON requests and direct Pydantic validation are unchanged.
### Breaking Changes
* 🐛 Treat empty scalar values as missing in form models. PR #16529 by @tiangolo.

item.description:
## Installation
```bash go install github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/cmd/wails@v2.17.0 ```
## Changes
### Security
- Windows notifications no longer fall back to PowerShell when the WinRT toast API fails; the error is returned instead - `wails init` now warns that remote templates are code: the `frontend:*` commands in `wails.json` and the scripts they call run during `wails build` and `wails dev`. The warning lists the commands found in the generated `wails.json` and is also shown with `-q`. The template docs now describe this trust boundary. - Hardened the `wails dev` server against cross-origin and DNS-rebinding attacks on the IPC WebSocket. item.title: [pnpm/pnpm] pnpm 12.14.0 (v12.14.0)
item.description:
This release adds the `sideEffectsCache.exclude` setting, stops `pnpm install` from waiting on the daily update check, and keeps pnpm from aborting with a core dump when the reader of its output exits.
### Minor Changes
- Added the `sideEffectsCache.exclude` setting for packages whose build depends on something pnpm cannot include in the cache key, such as the system libraries a native addon links against. pnpm builds the listed packages in every project and never restores or saves their builds through the side-effects cache, locally or on a `remoteCache` server. Under the global virtual store, each project gets its own copy of these packages and of the packages that depend on them. Entries use the same `name`, `@scope/*`, and `name@version` patterns as `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` #5271.
- `pnpm login` now prints the `npm-notice` response header during web-based login. Registries use it to show the verification code that completes the sign-in in the browser.

item.title: [sindresorhus/got] v16.1.0
item.description:
This release is the result of a large bug hunt. Many of the fixes make Got match its documented behavior, so you may notice some of them:
- Invalid options now throw: an empty `method`, a negative or fractional `maxRedirects` or `retry.limit`, a `prefixUrl` with a query string or fragment, and a `handlers` entry that is not a function. - A stream with a `body`, `json`, or `form` option now rejects writes, as documented. - The promise `response` event now only fires for the final response, not for every retry attempt. - `got.extend({body})` (and `json`, `form`) no longer sends the payload with every request of the instance. item.title: [anomalyco/opentui] Release v0.6.0 (v0.6.0)
item.description:
OpenTUI 0.5 kept the renderable tree in JavaScript. On each frame, JavaScript walked the tree and read each node's position back from Yoga. It then made one native call for each draw, so the cost of a frame grew with the number of nodes and draws. In 0.6.0, native code owns the tree. Each `Renderable` has a node in a native _scene_, which holds the node's Yoga node and paint state. Layout and paint setters stage their changes, and Core sends all staged changes to native code in one call before each frame step. Native code then lays out, clips, and paints the scene and fills the hit grid. It draws most built-in renderables without a call to JavaScript. When no visible node has a JavaScript hook, one native frame step lays out and paints the whole frame. Rendering pipeline follows a complete frame.
The built-in renderables and the React and Solid bindings keep their option names, but a few option values now throw, such as `enableLayout: false`. Custom renderables may need a little work.

## 🧰 WebMCP
New page.webmcp and frame.webmcp give access to the tools that a page registers through the experimental WebMCP browser API, so you can test them like any other part of your app:
```js const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ['--enable-features=WebMCP'] }); const page = await browser.newPage; await page.goto('');
for (const tool of await page.webmcp.tools) console.log(tool.name, tool.description);
const result = await page.webmcp.callTool('add', { a: 2, b: 40 }); console.log(result.content[0].text); // "42" ```

Four security vulnerabilities have been identified, and fixed, in this release. Users are advised to update gh to version `v2.102.0` as soon as possible.
`gh release download`, `gh run download`, `gh repo read-file --output`, and `gh attestation download` could write remote content to an unintended local file when the destination contained symbolic links.

item.description:
## 7.7.0 (2026-09-28)
The MongoDB Node.js team is pleased to announce version 7.7.0 of the `mongodb` package!
## Release Notes
### OIDC authentication recovers from a failed token fetch
A single failed OIDC token fetch, such as a cloud metadata endpoint timing out, used to leave the driver's token-fetch mutex holding that failure. Every later operation on the affected `MongoClient` then failed with the original error without attempting a new token fetch, and only restarting the process restored authentication. A failed token fetch now affects only the operation that triggered it.
### Driver dependencies updates
Dependency version changes: - `bson`: 7.2.0 -> 7.3.2 - `mongodb-connection-string-url`: 7.0.1 -> 7.0.2 - `mongodb-js/saslprep`: 1.4.11 -> 1.5.0
